findings.F1: The book's Calmar of 0.44 fails because of long, deep falls while it stays long: the book was long on 73% of coin-bars. Its deepest fall reached -82.5%, measured over the windows run end to end. In w14 the book lost 68.9% with every coin down 41% to 84%. In w7 it lost 43.9% and in w9 47.1%, with five or six of the six coins losing.
findings.F2: Held days whose close is below the 20-day mean earn nothing, while days well above it carry the gain. The two lowest quintiles of held coin-days by close/MA20 have next-day book returns of -0.0005 (t -0.48, n 2254) and -0.0005 (t -0.58, n 2254). The two highest quintiles have +0.0039 (t 2.97, n 2254) and +0.0070 (t 3.25, n 2254). These are pooled coin-days, not the book's daily mean over coins.
findings.F3: The drift lives only next to the high. On non-overlapping 10-bar samples of held bars, the excess return over the coin's all-window mean is +0.035 (t 2.73, n 266) when the close is within about 1.9% of its 20-day high. In the three quartiles further below the high it is -0.006 to -0.010 (t -0.73 to -1.19, n 266 to 267 each).
findings.F4: Held days with a falling 50-day average carry almost none of the book's gain. These 3695 held coin-days have a mean next-day book return of 0.0001 and contribute 0.08 of summed per-coin book return. The 5456 held days with a rising 50-day average have a mean of 0.0042 and contribute 3.84. This split is pooled coin-days, not the book's daily mean over coins.
findings.F5: The book's gain comes from a few long trades, and the many short ones lose (trades summed per trade, not book days). Of 3269 long trades, the median net return is -2.5% and 41% win. The 722 trades of 7 days or less average -4.85%, and those of 7 to 19 days average about -3.5%. The 620 trades longer than 29 days average +32.7%.
findings.F6: Entries made with the close below the 50-day average lose. These trades average -5.7% (median -7.4%, 27.5% winners, n 305), against +3.0% to +6.4% for the other quintiles.

ideas.idea: After a coin's new 20-day closing high, its excess rise over the following days appears only while its close stays within a small distance of that high and above its 20-day average. Once the close falls below its 20-day average, the coin's following returns are at or below its average.
ideas.consequence: Refuse to hold a breakout long once the coin has closed below its 20-day average, which removes the flat-to-losing held days inside the falls.
ideas.name: drift only near high

ideas.idea: The rise after a new 20-day closing high is larger when the coin's 50-day average is rising at that bar's close than when it is falling.
ideas.consequence: Take breakout longs only when the 50-day average is rising, and stay flat through the falling-average stretches that make up the deep windows.
ideas.name: breakouts need rising trend

ideas.idea: A new 20-day closing high made while the close is still below the coin's 50-day average is followed by returns below the coin's average over the next days.
ideas.consequence: Treat highs made under a falling or overhead 50-day average as failed rallies and refuse them, cutting the many short losing trades.
ideas.name: highs under trend fail
